title: A meta-analysis of the effect of generative AI on productivity and learning in programming
abstract: Across 23 studies and 27 effects, reported productivity gains are moderate (g=0.33), whereas the learning estimate is not statistically distinguishable from zero.
note: Method: meta-analysis. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (arXiv abstract, selection criteria, reported effect sizes and version history). Limitations: The search covers 2019-2025, not 2026 tools. Standardized effects combine unlike outcomes and cannot be read as percentage gains or evidence of equivalence in learning. Version: May 2026 v1 preprint; productivity 95% CI 0.09-0.58, learning g=0.14 with CI -0.18 to 0.47. No pooled effect is calculated by our review. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2605.04779

title: A multi-agent system for automating scientific discovery
abstract: Robin connects literature work, hypothesis generation and analysis to selected laboratory experiments in a multi-agent discovery workflow.
note: Method: experimental-demonstration. Status: peer-reviewed. Verification: content-checked (journal abstract and experimental scope). Limitations: A limited number of tasks and experiments; repeatable general discovery requires broader independent testing.

title: A New Look at AI's Impact on Jobs: Firm-Level AI Spending and Workforce Adjustment
abstract: Links firm AI spending and workforce records, finding stronger hiring among high-intensity adopters than among comparison firms.
note: Method: observational. Status: vendor-working-paper. Verification: content-checked (public paper and accompanying analysis). Limitations: Growing, larger, technical and venture-backed adopters differ before treatment; spending intensity is not a randomized intervention.

title: A Risk-Adaptive and Evidence-Constrained Framework for Generative AI Feedback in Programming Education
abstract: Combines risk prediction, evidence-bounded feedback and progressive assistance using historical failed submissions from 215 students.
note: Method: retrospective-computational. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (abstract and full HTML research-design section). Limitations: Retrospective prediction and message evaluation; no prospective demonstration of better unaided learning. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2609.29874

title: Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist
abstract: Co-Scientist generates and prioritizes research hypotheses, with selected results assessed through expert and experimental validation.
note: Method: benchmark-and-experimental-validation. Status: peer-reviewed. Verification: content-checked (journal abstract and validation description). Limitations: Selected biological cases and human direction; broad autonomy is not demonstrated.

title: Adoption and Impact of Command-Line AI Coding Agents: A Study of Microsoft's Early 2026 Rollout of Claude Code and GitHub Copilot CLI
abstract: Microsoft's early-2026 CLI-agent rollout is associated with roughly 24% more merged pull requests among adopters across four months.
note: Method: observational. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (primary abstract). Limitations: Merged PRs are a proxy rather than value; adoption spreads through social networks and is not random. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2607.01418

title: AI Impact on Engineering Productivity: 2026 Report Data
abstract: Vendor telemetry reports higher output alongside larger changes, review pressure, defects and incidents as AI adoption intensifies.
note: Method: observational. Status: vendor-report. Verification: content-checked (primary report overview; numerical details require report-specific denominator checks). Limitations: Selection, changing workflows, relative metrics, limited baselines, and vendor interests impede causal attribution.

title: AI is removing the middle class of software engineering
abstract: Proposes that cheaper implementation shifts engineering value toward judgment and responsibility, potentially hollowing out intermediate roles.
note: Method: commentary. Status: expert-blog. Verification: content-checked (primary essay). Limitations: An argued hypothesis, not a measured labor-market result or established forecast.

title: An AI system to help scientists write expert-level empirical software
abstract: ERA iteratively searches software candidates for scorable scientific and engineering tasks, demonstrating strong empirical-software performance.
note: Method: benchmark. Status: peer-reviewed. Verification: content-checked (journal abstract and task design). Limitations: Task and evaluator design are provided by people; benchmark gains do not automatically establish a new scientific explanation.

title: Artificial Intelligence in the Firm: Bottlenecks in Software Production
abstract: Firm-level adoption analysis using Jellyfish data finds increased coding activity, longer review cycles, and limited pass-through to resolved issues or epics.
note: Method: quasi-experiment. Status: working-paper. Verification: content-checked (author PDF, abstract, introduction, review analysis and sample table). Limitations: Proprietary data, parallel-trends assumptions, firm-level adoption, and output proxies; insignificant effects are not proof of exactly zero benefit. Version: Current linked version August 4, 2026; first version January 7, 2026.

title: Artificial intelligence tools expand scientists’ impact but contract science’s focus
abstract: Analysis of 41.3 million papers associates AI use with individual career and output advantages but a narrower collective distribution of research topics.
note: Method: observational. Status: peer-reviewed. Verification: content-checked (journal abstract and publication metadata). Limitations: Broad historical AI, not just LLMs; classifier and selection effects prevent a simple causal reading.

title: Automated Researchers Can Mitigate Well-Characterized Alignment Failures
abstract: Automated researchers improve benchmarks for ten defined alignment failures, with selected transfer and behavioral auditing tests.
note: Method: benchmark-and-experimental-validation. Status: vendor-research-report. Verification: content-checked (technical report, evaluation protocol and caveats). Limitations: Unequal iterative opportunities in the human comparison, selective capability tests, and vendor-produced evidence; detected cheating trajectories were excluded.

title: Beyond Productivity: Measuring Developers' Cognitive Load During GenAI-Supported Software Development
abstract: A four-day study of 21 SAP developers relates perceived cognitive load to AI use and task context; wearable measurements add limited information.
note: Method: field-observation. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (primary abstract only). Limitations: Small nonrandom sample and short observation; does not establish an overall causal increase or reduction in mental effort. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2609.37645

title: Beyond the Commit: Developer Perspectives on Productivity with AI Coding Assistants
abstract: A BNY Mellon survey with 2,989 responses and 11 interviews argues for measuring expertise, ownership and longer-run productivity alongside activity.
note: Method: mixed-methods. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (primary abstract). Limitations: Self-reports within one organization; identifies constructs rather than a causal effect size. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2602.03593

title: Can AI automate AI R&D yet?
abstract: An end-to-end test of novel post-training research finds weak improvements relative to a withheld human method and exposes misleading result selection.
note: Method: benchmark. Status: organization-report. Verification: content-checked (full report including methods, results and limitations). Limitations: One task, few expensive runs, partly human scope assessment, and contamination in successor models.

title: Canaries in the Gold Mine: Early Productivity Gains from Artificial Intelligence Creating Organization Capital
abstract: Firm-level AI-skilled employment measures link recent productivity improvements to investment in durable organizational knowledge and processes.
note: Method: observational. Status: working-paper. Verification: content-checked (publisher abstract and scope). Limitations: Broader AI than chatbots, employment-based investment proxies and identification assumptions; not a license-purchase ROI estimate.

title: Characterizing the Quality Profile of AI-Generated C++ in Production
abstract: Production C++ telemetry finds distinct warning profiles, added review effort, and higher compute consumption in the studied AI-code cohort.
note: Method: observational. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (primary abstract and study scope). Limitations: One enterprise and language, attribution challenges, private data; the result is not a universal defect or cost multiplier. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2608.06640

title: ChatGPT's impact on student learning outcomes: a meta-analysis of 35 experimental studies
abstract: A synthesis of 35 studies and 4,193 participants reports a positive standardized learning effect (g=0.670) and no detected publication bias in its tests.
note: Method: meta-analysis. Status: peer-reviewed. Verification: content-checked (publisher abstract, bibliographic metadata and stated study window). Limitations: Underlying studies date from 2022-2024. Mixed cognitive and non-cognitive outcomes, selection and limited moderators constrain comparison with newer STEM syntheses; non-detection does not establish absence of bias.

title: Checkpoints Are Not Enough: Trust Calibration in CoSLR, a Human-AI System for Systematic Literature Reviews
abstract: A 63-participant evaluation of an AI-assisted review system finds that mandatory verification checkpoints alone do not ensure users actually check generated synthesis.
note: Method: survey-demonstration. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (arXiv abstract, participant count and reported verification-intention result). Limitations: Short interaction and self-reported intentions, not a controlled estimate of review accuracy or error prevention. Useful as a process warning, not validation of this review. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2609.22248

title: Claude-shaped science
abstract: BootLoops connects methods across quantitative fields; domain experts redirect technically correct results toward questions with scientific significance.
note: Method: case-study. Status: vendor-hosted-essay. Verification: content-checked (full essay and disclosure). Limitations: Selected personal case studies and manuscripts under further verification; the author was a visiting researcher at Anthropic.

title: DarwinX: Evolving Agent Harnesses Through Natural Selection
abstract: Population search over harnesses improves benchmark performance with a frozen model, treating tools, prompts and control flow as evolvable components.
note: Method: benchmark. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (primary abstract). Limitations: Recent author-reported benchmark results require independent replication and careful train-test separation. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2608.07545

title: Does Fixing Break Security? An Empirical Study of Security Degradation in Iterative LLM-Driven Infrastructure-as-Code Repair
abstract: Iterative infrastructure-code repair can regress security; changing the regression definition reduces measured affected scenarios from 13.8% to 3.3%.
note: Method: benchmark-analysis. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (primary abstract and measurement definitions). Limitations: Validator semantics and resource restructuring influence apparent regressions; cumulative-best metrics conceal intermediate failures. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2608.13404

title: DORA | Balancing AI tensions: Moving from AI adoption to effective SDLC use
abstract: Discusses tensions between AI adoption, trust, verification, workflow design, and effective use across the software lifecycle.
note: Method: commentary. Status: organization-analysis. Verification: content-checked (primary analysis). Limitations: Interpretive and practical guidance; not a new randomized productivity estimate.

title: Evidence of impact and interpretational limits of generative AI in STEM education: a systematic review and meta-analysis on cognitive learning outcomes
abstract: A STEM synthesis finds highly heterogeneous positive conventional estimates; robust Bayesian publication-bias adjustment reduces the overall mean close to zero.
note: Method: meta-analysis. Status: peer-reviewed. Verification: content-checked (publisher abstract, search protocol, risk-of-bias appendices and bias-adjustment discussion). Limitations: 85 eligible studies, 49 pooled, 59 effects; I-squared=96.32%. Bias correction depends on modeling assumptions and does not prove that every instructional use fails.

title: Fragmented Markers, Mixed Results: A Systematic Review of AI Coding Assistants and Developer Productivity
abstract: A two-stage SPACE-informed review identifies 187 distinct productivity-related markers and finds more favorable patterns in perceived than objectively evaluated outcomes.
note: Method: systematic-review. Status: peer-reviewed-conference. Verification: content-checked (official conference abstract and author PDF methodology, source policy and discussion sections). Limitations: Marker frequencies and reported effect directions are not pooled effect magnitudes. Diverse settings, confounders and source types limit universal conclusions. Version: ASE 2026 accepted research paper with an accessible author preprint in a July-dated URL directory; first posting date not independently established. Presentation scheduled 14 October, after our cutoff; no claim is based on a future presentation.

title: Generative AI and the Redefinition of Entry-Level Software Work
abstract: U.S. vacancy data show a relative decline in junior software openings and higher experience requirements after ChatGPT's release.
note: Method: quasi-experiment. Status: working-paper. Verification: content-checked (primary discussion-paper abstract). Limitations: Vacancies and posting requirements are not headcount or direct measures of individual AI substitution.

title: How AI Impacts Skill Formation
abstract: Randomized study of learning a programming library finds reduced conceptual understanding, code reading and debugging with AI assistance on average.
note: Method: experiment. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (primary abstract and preregistered design description). Limitations: A small task-specific study; interaction-pattern subgroups are exploratory and not separately randomized. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2601.20245

title: How Artificial Intelligence Shapes Science: Evidence from AlphaFold
abstract: AlphaFold structure availability appears to complement experimental biology and expand basic research on previously understudied proteins, without comparable downstream drug-development effects so far.
note: Method: observational. Status: working-paper. Verification: content-checked (current publisher abstract). Limitations: Domain-specific transition and observation window; predicted structures do not settle biological function or translational success.

title: LLAMA LIMA: A Living Meta-Analysis on the Effects of Generative AI on Learning Mathematics
abstract: A regularly updated mathematics-learning synthesis reports a positive estimate in its September v5, with larger effects for teacher-supplementing and longer interventions.
note: Method: living-meta-analysis. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (version-specific arXiv abstract and revision history; underlying trial extraction not independently checked). Limitations: 34 studies in v5; narrower eligibility and Bayesian models differ from broad STEM syntheses. Shared trials are not independent corroboration; a credible interval is not a confidence interval. Version: Pinned to v5 (11 September 2026): g=0.57, credible interval 0.36-0.79. DOI identifies the version family; January first-submission and September revision dates must not be conflated. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2601.18685

title: Measurements for understanding the pace of AI development inside frontier labs
abstract: A prototype internal R&D index distinguishes AI assistance, collaboration and leadership from full autonomy using a fixed task basket.
note: Method: observational. Status: vendor-report. Verification: content-checked (full methods and index interpretation). Limitations: Model-rated internal documentation and approximate time weights; automation share is not research speedup or independent safety evidence.

title: Measuring the Self-Reported Impact of Early-2026 AI on Technical Worker Productivity
abstract: A survey of 349 technical workers estimates perceived changes in the value of work, extending beyond time saved on fixed tasks.
note: Method: survey. Status: organization-report. Verification: content-checked (organization report and sample description). Limitations: Self-reported counterfactuals, selection, and unusually technical respondents; not independently measured causal uplift.

title: OECD Digital Education Outlook 2026: Exploring Effective Uses of Generative AI in Education
abstract: OECD distinguishes stronger assisted task performance from learning that persists without AI, emphasizing instructional design and pedagogical intent.
note: Method: policy-evidence-synthesis. Status: organization-report. Verification: content-checked (official summary, key messages and bibliographic details; not all 267 pages). Limitations: A policy and expert synthesis rather than one causal trial; instructional examples do not establish that every tutor or classroom intervention works.

title: Olympiad-level formal mathematical reasoning with reinforcement learning
abstract: AlphaProof combines reinforcement learning with formal mathematical reasoning and machine-checked proofs at olympiad level.
note: Method: benchmark. Status: peer-reviewed. Verification: content-checked (journal abstract and stated evaluation scope). Limitations: Formalized, bounded tasks and substantial infrastructure; proof validity does not establish the value or novelty of an arbitrary question.

title: Patterns of Learner-AI Interaction and Academic Performance in an Object-Oriented Programming Course
abstract: Among 210 first-year OOP students, different self-reported AI-use profiles did not significantly differ in unaided assessment performance.
note: Method: survey. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (primary abstract). Limitations: One course, nonrandom use and self-report; a null comparison is not equivalence or proof that pedagogy does not matter. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2607.24755

title: ResearchGym: Evaluating Language Model Agents on Real-World AI Research
abstract: Five research environments expose a gap between occasional strong research results and reliable completion of long research workflows.
note: Method: benchmark. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (primary abstract). Limitations: Small number of environments, configuration sensitivity and model vintage; workshop acceptance is distinct from main-conference acceptance. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2602.15112

title: SWE-CI: Evaluating Agent Capabilities in Maintaining Codebases via Continuous Integration
abstract: Evaluates agents across successive repository changes rather than a single static issue, making regression and maintainability central outcomes.
note: Method: benchmark. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (primary abstract). Limitations: A benchmark environment and curated tasks; longitudinal agent evaluation is not longitudinal organizational evaluation. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2603.03823

title: Test Coverage Analysis of Agentic Pull Requests
abstract: Coverage measurements on 4,882 agent PRs show incomplete execution of changed lines and uneven benefits from agent-written tests.
note: Method: observational. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (primary abstract). Limitations: Coverage is not assertion quality; the AIDev corpus overlaps other studies and should not be counted as independent replication. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2607.18057

title: The 2026 AI Index Report

author.family: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence

abstract: An annual cross-domain reference compendium links technical capability, economic indicators, science, education, governance and public opinion to underlying datasets.
note: Method: cross-domain-evidence-compendium. Status: organization-report. Verification: content-checked (official 2026 landing page, chapter descriptions and top takeaways; report not read in full). Limitations: Indicators mix benchmarks, surveys, estimates and observational series with different dates and denominators. Adoption, investment and benchmark scores are not interchangeable with causal productivity gains.

title: The Changing Landscape of Postsecondary Education
abstract: Fall 2025 U.S. enrollments fall in traditional Computer and Information Science while Data Science and Analytics grow.
note: Method: administrative-observation. Status: organization-report. Verification: content-checked (primary administrative-data summary). Limitations: Enrollment shifts do not identify AI-driven motivation and can include changes in program labels and international flows.

title: The Devil Is in the Interface: Evaluating How Tool Architecture Shapes Coding Agent Behavior
abstract: Across 11,700 trajectories, different tool architectures alter coding-agent behavior, consistency and token consumption despite similar available actions.
note: Method: benchmark-experiment. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (primary abstract). Limitations: Repository-issue tasks and selected actors; efficiency within this evaluation is not a firm-level productivity estimate. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2608.11386

title: The Impact of AI Coding Assistants on Software Engineering: A Longitudinal Study
abstract: A six-month survey panel reports a shift toward supervisory engineering work and growing experience-related costs despite stable perceived productivity gains.
note: Method: longitudinal-survey. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (primary abstract). Limitations: Perceived effects, attrition and 95 matched participants; not independently timed task performance. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2605.23135

title: The impact of GenAI on jobs, productivity and work organization: a review of the empirical evidence
abstract: ILO connects task gains with weaker aggregate-output evidence, employment distribution and changes in coordination and job quality.
note: Method: narrative-review. Status: organization-report. Verification: content-checked (publisher summary and PDF introduction and productivity section). Limitations: A research brief synthesizing heterogeneous studies, not an independent experiment or meta-analytic estimate. Early null aggregate effects do not establish permanent absence of benefit. Version: The publisher page dates publication 1 June 2026; the eight-page PDF is headed May 2026. Crossref uses the shorter title without the review subtitle for the same publisher-supplied DOI. These are the same brief, not separate evidence.

title: Towards end-to-end automation of AI research
abstract: Demonstrates an extended automated ML-research workflow and evaluation of generated work through workshop peer review.
note: Method: benchmark. Status: peer-reviewed. Verification: content-checked (journal abstract and primary publication description). Limitations: Human selection and workshop-level assessment are not evidence of unrestricted autonomous scientific excellence.

title: Twelve Ways to Be Wrong About AI-Assisted Coding
abstract: Organizes recurring methodological mistakes in claims about AI-assisted coding and the measurement of productivity.
note: Method: commentary. Status: expert-blog. Verification: content-checked (primary essay). Limitations: Critical expert commentary, not an independent outcome study.

title: Uber Caps Usage of AI Tools Like Claude Code to Manage Costs
abstract: Discusses reported limits on Uber's coding-agent spending and the mismatch between token consumption and demonstrable customer value.
note: Method: commentary-on-reporting. Status: expert-blog. Verification: content-checked (primary commentary and linked reporting). Limitations: Commentary on reporting; not an audited cost-benefit analysis of Uber.

title: UK higher education student numbers fall for second year in a row
abstract: UK 2024/25 official data show growth in Computing and AI despite a decline in total student numbers.
note: Method: administrative-observation. Status: official-statistics. Verification: content-checked (official statistical release as indexed by the publisher). Limitations: Different period and classification from U.S. figures; a geographic contrast rather than direct refutation.

title: Vero: Can AI Agents Build Formally Verified Software Repositories?
abstract: Joint implementation-and-proof generation succeeds on 27 of 43 curated multi-module Lean repositories in the strongest evaluated configuration, with no complete success on the hardest cases.
note: Method: benchmark. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (primary abstract). Limitations: Formal validity is conditional on specification; small curated benchmark and configuration-dependent result. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2608.13522

title: We are Changing our Developer Productivity Experiment Design
abstract: METR's follow-up describes selection and measurement problems as developers increasingly decline AI-disallowed work and operate agents concurrently.
note: Method: experiment-update. Status: organization-report. Verification: content-checked (full methodological update). Limitations: Raw later estimates are explicitly treated as unreliable; they neither erase the original trial nor establish a new precise productivity effect.

title: Writing Code vs. Shipping Code: Productivity Effects Across Generations of AI Coding Tools
abstract: A matched event study of more than 500,000 developers finds large cumulative commit effects that attenuate for projects, releases, and application usage.
note: Method: observational. Status: working-paper. Verification: content-checked (current publisher abstract and revision metadata). Limitations: Nonrandom adoption, heterogeneous tools and outcomes; cumulative event-study estimates are not daily speedup percentages. Version: September 2026 revision; first issued May 2026.

title: Your Programming Students' Cognition with ChatGPT: Higher Performance, Lower Retention, and Reduced Ownership
abstract: Students assisted by ChatGPT produced stronger C solutions but showed lower immediate and 48-hour recall, with no significant difference in the rate of forgetting.
note: Method: experiment. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (primary abstract, full HTML methods and results). Limitations: 55 analyzed participants, three tasks and 48-hour follow-up; substantial physiological missingness. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2609.21194

title: AI Copilot Code Quality: 2025 Look Back at 12 Months of Data
abstract: Tracks code-change patterns, duplication and moved-code metrics across the period of expanding AI-assistant adoption.
note: Method: observational. Status: vendor-report. Verification: content-checked (primary report page and stated metric definitions). Limitations: Calendar-time association is not treatment identification; moved-code measures are not the entirety of refactoring.

title: AI | 2025 Stack Overflow Developer Survey
abstract: High reported use or planned use coexists with greater distrust than trust of AI accuracy and widespread frustration with nearly correct answers.
note: Method: survey. Status: organization-report. Verification: content-checked (AI section including exact question wording). Limitations: Opt-in survey and question-specific denominators; planned use is not adoption, and frustration is not measured net time loss.

title: AI-Assisted Programming Decreases the Productivity of Experienced Developers by Increasing the Technical Debt and Maintenance Burden
abstract: An open-source study reports greater activity among peripheral contributors alongside added review and rework burdens for core contributors.
note: Method: observational. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (current primary abstract). Limitations: Contributor seniority proxies and observational adoption; review redistribution is not itself proof of lost total value. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2510.10165

title: AlphaEvolve: A coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery
abstract: An evolutionary coding agent improves algorithms and infrastructure through evaluator-driven search, including selected novel mathematical procedures.
note: Method: experimental-demonstration. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (primary abstract). Limitations: Developer white paper, selected demonstrations and human-defined evaluators; no universal research-autonomy claim follows. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2506.13131

title: Assessing the Quality and Security of AI-Generated Code: A Quantitative Analysis
abstract: Static analysis of 4,442 Java assignments finds that passing functional tests does not reliably indicate broader code quality or security.
note: Method: benchmark-analysis. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (primary abstract). Limitations: Assignments, selected models, and analyzer findings are not direct observations of production exploitation. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2508.14727

title: Canaries in the Coal Mine? Six Facts about the Recent Employment Effects of Artificial Intelligence - Stanford Digital Economy Lab
abstract: U.S. payroll evidence documents disproportionate early-career employment weakness in highly AI-exposed occupations.
note: Method: observational. Status: working-paper. Verification: content-checked (primary publication page and stated research design). Limitations: Exposure, age, and employment trends do not uniquely identify AI as the cause; versions and panel construction change estimates.

title: Darwin Godel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
abstract: Darwin Godel Machine evolves the code of coding agents using an archive and external benchmarks while retaining a foundation model as the engine.
note: Method: benchmark. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (primary abstract). Limitations: Agent-code improvement is not autonomous selection of goals or demonstrated unbounded improvement of model intelligence. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2505.22954

title: Discovering state-of-the-art reinforcement learning algorithms
abstract: Automated discovery of reinforcement-learning rules yields methods competitive with hand-designed algorithms and tested in additional environments.
note: Method: benchmark. Status: peer-reviewed. Verification: content-checked (journal abstract and evaluation description). Limitations: Search objective, environments and compute allocation are human-designed; transfer has a defined scope.

title: DORA 2025 State of AI-assisted Software Development Report
abstract: The 2025 report interprets AI as an amplifier of existing organizational capabilities and weaknesses.
note: Method: survey. Status: organization-report. Verification: content-checked (research publication page and report synthesis). Limitations: Organizational associations do not imply that mature practices guarantee positive outcomes for every adoption.

title: From AI for Science to Agentic Science: A Survey on Autonomous Scientific Discovery
abstract: A domain-oriented survey organizes scientific agents across life sciences, chemistry, materials and physics using capability, workflow and autonomy frameworks.
note: Method: technical-survey. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (version-specific arXiv abstract, framework description and authorship metadata). Limitations: A taxonomy and narrative synthesis, not a causal estimate of research productivity or evidence that agents achieve reliable general scientific autonomy. Version: Pinned to October 2025 v2; a taxonomy of scientific agency must not be confused with validation of every system it surveys. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2508.14111

title: Generative AI and Sales Productivity: Field Experiments in Online Retail
abstract: Retail experiments across seven workflows report heterogeneous sales effects, primarily through conversion rather than basket value.
note: Method: experiment. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (current primary abstract). Limitations: One platform, 2023-2024 interventions and short-run sales measures; not aggregate total-factor productivity. Version: June 29, 2026 revision; earlier title referred to firm productivity. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2510.12049

title: Generative AI at Work
abstract: A staggered workplace deployment increased customer issues resolved per hour by 15% on average, with greater benefits for less experienced workers.
note: Method: quasi-experiment. Status: peer-reviewed. Verification: content-checked (journal abstract and introduction). Limitations: One customer-support environment; assistance is embedded in a specific workflow. The published estimate differs from the earlier 14% working-paper figure.

title: Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning
abstract: A school mathematics trial distinguishes AI-assisted practice from unaided assessment and shows the importance of tutor guardrails for preserving learning.
note: Method: experiment. Status: peer-reviewed. Verification: content-checked (publisher abstract and experiment description). Limitations: Mathematics education and a specific instructional implementation; not a result for every tutor or subject.
container-title: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

title: Human-Written vs. AI-Generated Code: A Large-Scale Study of Defects, Vulnerabilities, and Complexity
abstract: Compares more than 500,000 Python and Java samples and identifies different defect, vulnerability and structural-complexity profiles in human and model code.
note: Method: benchmark-analysis. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (primary abstract). Limitations: Sample construction and static classification affect comparison; simpler code is not necessarily safer or more maintainable. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2508.21634

title: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
abstract: Experienced maintainers took 19% longer on tasks in familiar repositories when allowed early-2025 AI tools, despite expecting and perceiving speedups.
note: Method: experiment. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (primary paper abstract and linked experiment report). Limitations: A small, expert population and a specific model/tool vintage; not an estimate for 2026 agents. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2507.09089

title: Still Waters, Rapid Currents: Early Labor Market Transformation under Generative AI
abstract: Danish adoption surveys linked to administrative records reveal task reorganization but limited early average effects on earnings or recorded hours.
note: Method: quasi-experiment. Status: working-paper. Verification: content-checked (current publisher abstract and revision metadata). Limitations: Denmark's institutions, short horizon and averages; null aggregate effects can coexist with occupational transitions. Version: March 2026 revision of May 2025 working paper.

title: Teaching with AI: A Systematic Review of Chatbots, Generative Tools, and Tutoring Systems in Programming Education
abstract: A review of 58 programming-education studies groups chatbots, generative tools and intelligent tutors, describing benefits alongside overreliance and implementation barriers.
note: Method: systematic-review. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (arXiv v2 abstract and related-publication metadata). Limitations: The categories include non-generative tutoring systems. Percentages describe included studies, not prevalence among learners or developers; no common pooled effect is established. Version: December 2025 arXiv v2; associated 2026 journal DOI 10.26803/ijlter.25.1.1 is not independent evidence. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2510.03884

title: The Effects of Generative AI on High-Skilled Work: Evidence from Three Field Experiments with Software Developers
abstract: Three workplace experiments covering 4,867 developers report a pooled increase of about 26% in completed tasks following access to coding assistance.
note: Method: experiment. Status: research-publication. Verification: content-checked (research publication page and reported pooled result). Limitations: Completed-task measures vary across firms; access, actual use, quality, and commercial value are distinct.

title: The effects of generative AI on productivity, innovation and entrepreneurship
abstract: OECD synthesis connects experimental productivity evidence with innovation, entrepreneurship, user expertise and task fit.
note: Method: narrative-review. Status: organization-working-paper. Verification: content-checked (official abstract, bibliographic details and stated review scope; not all 59 pages). Limitations: A selective review, not a pooled causal effect; longer-run organizational outcomes remain weakly established. Primary trials overlap with this review's evidence.

title: The Fast and Spurious: Developer Productivity with GenAI
abstract: A survey of 415 practitioners maps perceived gains and shifted effort across SPACE dimensions, including review and verification costs.
note: Method: survey. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (current primary abstract). Limitations: Self-report and adoption differences; neither proves net losses nor measures firm-level product value. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2510.24265

title: The Impact of LLM-Assistants on Software Developer Productivity: A Systematic Review and Mapping Study
abstract: A mapping of 39 peer-reviewed studies highlights multidimensional productivity assessment but scarce longitudinal and team-level evidence, with unresolved quality effects.
note: Method: systematic-review. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (arXiv v3 abstract and journal/version metadata). Limitations: Most included research is exploratory; positive study counts are not pooled causal effects. The July 2026 revision still synthesizes studies through December 2024. Version: Abstract appraised in arXiv v3, revised 31 July 2026. Related ACM publication DOI 10.1145/3809494 is the same work, not a replication. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2507.03156

title: The vibe coder's career path is doomed
abstract: Personal experience with agent-generated applications raises questions about retaining a mental model and building a sustainable development career.
note: Method: case-study. Status: expert-blog. Verification: content-checked (primary essay). Limitations: A selected experience and polemical argument; cannot establish prevalence or causation.

title: Artificial intelligence and illusions of understanding in scientific research
abstract: A conceptual taxonomy examines how AI's promises of productivity and objectivity can produce illusions of understanding and scientific monocultures.
note: Method: perspective. Status: peer-reviewed-perspective. Verification: content-checked (journal perspective abstract and metadata). Limitations: A theoretical perspective rather than an estimate of the incidence or size of effects.

title: DORA | Accelerate State of DevOps Report 2024
abstract: Organization-level research links AI use to individual benefits while reporting adverse associations with delivery stability and throughput in the 2024 sample.
note: Method: survey. Status: organization-report. Verification: content-checked (report landing page and primary organizational interpretation). Limitations: Survey-based relationships, self-selection and organizational context; not randomized deployment effects.

title: How much does AI impact development speed? An enterprise-based randomized controlled trial
abstract: A trial with 96 Google engineers estimated approximately 21% shorter task time with internal AI features.
note: Method: experiment. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (primary abstract and methods summary). Limitations: Wide uncertainty, one complex task, internal tooling; not an estimate for all engineering work. Version: 2024 preprint; associated ICSE 2025 Software Engineering in Practice presentation is catalogued separately. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2410.12944

title: Experimental evidence on the productivity effects of generative artificial intelligence
abstract: A preregistered experiment with 453 professionals found shorter completion times and higher assessed quality on occupational writing tasks with ChatGPT.
note: Method: experiment. Status: peer-reviewed. Verification: content-checked (publisher abstract and study description). Limitations: Short writing assignments and assessed artifacts; not long-run firm productivity.

title: Mathematical discoveries from program search with large language models
abstract: FunSearch pairs language-model proposals with systematic evaluation to find new cap-set constructions and improved bin-packing heuristics.
note: Method: experimental-demonstration. Status: peer-reviewed. Verification: content-checked (journal abstract and approach description). Limitations: A human-specified program representation and evaluator constrain the search; a domain result is not general research autonomy. Version: Published online December 2023; Nature volume 625 is dated 2024.

title: Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier: Field Experimental Evidence of the Effects of Artificial Intelligence on Knowledge Worker Productivity and Quality
abstract: An experiment with 758 consultants distinguishes tasks within the model's effective capability frontier from tasks on which AI assistance can worsen correctness.
note: Method: experiment. Status: author-manuscript. Verification: content-checked (author manuscript, methods and reported task contrast). Limitations: Task-specific frontier and 2023 GPT-4; do not infer present model limitations directly. Version: Study first circulated in 2023; linked author manuscript is a 2026 revision.

title: The Impact of AI on Developer Productivity: Evidence from GitHub Copilot
abstract: Developers given Copilot completed a JavaScript HTTP-server task in substantially less time; the reported reduction was 55.8%.
note: Method: experiment. Status: preprint. Verification: content-checked (primary abstract and experimental description). Limitations: An isolated task and early tool; completion-conditioned estimates and uncertainty matter. Persistent identifier: arXiv:2302.06590

title: Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold
abstract: Demonstrates highly accurate protein-structure prediction and establishes a foundational example of specialized AI supporting science.
note: Method: benchmark-and-experimental-validation. Status: peer-reviewed. Verification: content-checked (publisher abstract and bibliographic identity). Limitations: Predicted structure is not equivalent to experimentally established function, dynamics or drug efficacy.

title: The SPACE of Developer Productivity: There's More to It than You Think
abstract: Defines productivity through satisfaction, performance, activity, communication and collaboration, and efficiency and flow.
note: Method: framework. Status: research-framework. Verification: content-checked (primary framework description). Limitations: A measurement framework, not an AI-effect estimate; activity is one dimension rather than a complete measure. Version: ACM Queue uses the full subtitle; the same DOI's Crossref record uses The SPACE of Developer Productivity. Title, authors and 2021 publication year compared on 13 October 2026.
